audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition debt service is absent from the pre-acquisition owner-earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed Q2 2026 interest expense increased $37.1m year over year and H1 interest expense increased $52.6m; exact normalized annual mismatch unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE numerator retains interest expense, but the $460.6m anchor predates the acquisition financing while the bridge and share count are post-closing.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the amount of cash required to pay interest on our indebtedness following, subject to market conditions and other factors, completion of the debt financing and the Acquisition, and thus the demands on our cash resources, will materially increase as a result of the Term Loan Facility and the Acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a possibility. The latest 10-Q attributes the interest increase primarily to SPX FLOW financing. One quarter's $37.1m increase equals 8.1% of the anchor, so recurring post-closing interest is reasonably capable of changing modeled value. Excluding SPX FLOW earnings simultaneously understates value, but that does not cure the missing interest or make the current mixed-perimeter valuation self-consistent.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild normalized consolidated OE using post-closing SPX FLOW earnings, acquisition interest, taxes, working-capital needs and maintenance capex, then rerun all scenarios; alternatively rerun the legacy perimeter using pre-closing cash, debt and shares.

audit_findings.title: Post-closing claims ahead of common equity have not been established
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed preliminary SPX FLOW liabilities: $281.3m accounts payable and accrued liabilities, $96.2m contract liabilities, $593.0m deferred tax liability, $531.3m long-term debt and $109.0m other liabilities; residual exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any omitted senior claim would require a bridge deduction or reduce future consolidated OE; ordinary operating liabilities should instead remain reflected through operating cash requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: SPX FLOW may have liabilities that we failed, or were unable, to discover in the course of performing our due diligence investigations of SPX FLOW.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q now identifies substantial assumed liabilities, so their existence is established and the earlier parsing failure is no longer the full state of the record. However, purchase accounting remains provisional, the valuation does not show a claim-by-claim reconciliation, and unknown contingent liabilities remain possible. The record cannot determine whether any omitted amount is incremental to liabilities already captured through OE, debt or purchase consideration, so materiality remains unresolved rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every July 2026 liability and the final purchase-price allocation to debt, normalized OE and bridge treatment; obtain the final acquisition accounting and quantify indemnities, guarantees, pensions, environmental exposures and other non-debt senior claims without double counting operating liabilities.

audit_findings.title: Largely unfunded postretirement obligations may require cash beyond the expense retained in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $149.7m postretirement liability at July 4, 2026, equal to $1.65 per valuation share; 2025 contributions were $9.0m
audit_findings.mechanism: Benefit payments exceeding the periodic expense embedded in OE would reduce normalized OE; an obligation not otherwise captured could instead enter as a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Our postretirement plans are largely unfunded, and therefore plan contributions generally reflect required benefit payments.
audit_findings.explanation: A cash-versus-expense mismatch is demonstrated for the legacy plans: 2025 contributions were $9.0m while pension cost of $3.6m and other-benefit income of $3.6m netted to zero. Nevertheless, even treating the entire $149.7m post-closing liability as an incremental bridge deduction would reduce value by only $1.65 per share, about 1.9% of the $86.37 base value and 1.4% of the $117.96 gap to market price. It therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion, although double counting must be avoided because benefit expense and payments may already affect OE.
audit_findings.action: Compare annual OE pension and postretirement expense with cash contributions and benefit payments, including acquired plans, and incorporate only the persistent excess cash requirement in the next consolidated rerun.

audit_findings.title: Environmental remediation is an existing senior cash claim with material estimation risk
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $56.8m liability less $10.3m recovery asset = $46.5m recorded net claim; $97.0m high end less $10.3m asset = $86.7m, or $0.96 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Environmental payments reduce OE when expensed or paid; any existing obligation not captured in normalized OE requires a bridge deduction net of probable recoveries.
audit_findings.evidence: Our environmental reserve of $56.1 at December 31, 2025, represents management’s estimate of undiscounted costs expected to be incurred related to environmental assessment or remediation efforts, including related legal fees, without regard to potential recoveries from insurance companies or other third parties.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim and estimation risk are demonstrated, including $2.5m of acquired environmental liabilities. At the disclosed high end net of the recovery asset, the exposure is $86.7m, only 1.1% of the $7,817m base equity value and $0.96 per share versus a $117.96 market-price gap. It is therefore not capable of changing the valuation conclusion, though inconsistent treatment could modestly overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Trace environmental expense, $4.6m of H1 2026 payments and recoveries through OE, then deduct only the net obligation not already represented in normalized earnings or cash flows.

audit_findings.title: Recurring corporate-owned life-insurance gains may remain embedded in operating earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed gains of $6.1m, $4.6m and $4.2m in 2025-2023; filed COLI asset $142.0m, equal to $1.57 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained COLI gains inflate OE, while omission of the realizable COLI asset from the bridge understates non-operating asset value.
audit_findings.evidence: Gains from COLI investments of $ 6.1 , $ 4.6 , and $ 4.2 were recorded within General and administrative expenses in our Consolidated Statements of Operations during years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are demonstrated and recurring, but whether they were purged from OE is unresolved. The 2025 gain is only 1.3% of the $460.6m anchor, while the entire reported asset is only 1.8% of the $7,817m base equity value. Neither side of the inconsistency is large enough to change the conclusion that modeled value is far below the $204.33 market price.
audit_findings.action: Verify each OE year's treatment of COLI gains and related cash flows; rerun after either purging the gains and adding realizable net COLI value to the bridge or consistently excluding both.

audit_findings.title: The stated share-count ceiling is not a demonstrated maximum
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum PSU excess unquantified; 90.5m valuation shares exceed filed Q2 diluted shares of 89.8m by 0.7m
audit_findings.mechanism: Shares issued above the 90.5m denominator would dilute every scenario's per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: PSUs vest based on predetermined performance metrics that align with the Company's stock price and financial performance generally following a three-year performance period and are subject to a payout factor which includes a maximum and minimum payout.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation denominator includes a cushion over the filed diluted count, but the filing confirms that PSUs have an undisclosed maximum payout factor. Thus, describing 90.5m as an absolute ceiling is unsupported. The available record does not quantify maximum shares for all outstanding tranches, so it cannot establish whether the excess over 90.5m is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain every outstanding PSU agreement and the proxy award tables, calculate maximum settlement shares by tranche including vested-pending and anti-dilutive awards, and rerun per-share values if the total exceeds 90.5m.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed/computed FY2020 residual $29.0m, 25.8% of filed D&A and 6.3% of the $460.6m anchor; eligible portion and full-series impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to historical OE and could raise the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $29.0m (25.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement error is demonstrated because the unidentified amount was retained as an expense. The treatment is conservative, but classification is unresolved. The disclosed FY2020 residual is meaningful relative to that year's $105.0m OE, while the record supplies neither eligible residuals for every anchor year nor enough classification evidence to establish the resulting trend-anchor effect. Materiality therefore remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Classify residual D&A by asset and economic function for every OE year, document which amounts are genuinely non-economic and not offset by maintenance capex, then recompute the historical OE series, log-trend anchor and all scenarios.
